messages:
mina: quick profiling update from the 8xA100 cluster, tp=8 runs with dynamic seq lengths. seeing ~10-14% extra GPU memory used that looks like comm/shadow buffers + per-shard temp staging. flamegraph attached (summary below).

alex: can you paste the peak mem breakdown? is it NCCL comm buffers specifically or staging for async copies?

mina: pasted perf numbers from nvprof and our internal tracer:
```
Total GPU used: 64000 MiB
Model weights + kv cache: 49000 MiB
TP shard overhead: 3200 MiB
NCCL comm buffers (persistent + ephemeral): 4200 MiB
Staging/async temp slabs: 3800 MiB
Allocator free fragmentation estimate: ~5% (~2500 MiB)
```

sam: hmm. comm buffers 4.2GB seems high. are we allocating per-rank per-stream double buffers? we do 2x for double-buffered collectives. also many small temp buffers get separate cudaMallocs which fragment.

leo: +1 on fragmentation. I noticed our per-request workspace path calls cudaMalloc for <1MB chunks when sequence length jumps. allocator isn't coalescing.

alex: does kv cache contribute to duplication? when we shard TP we sometimes create local views vs copies.

mina: yes — for batched prefix cases the KV cache code currently creates shadow copies on each shard during rollouts to avoid cross-shard synchronization. that was cheap for small seq but with long prefixes it's not.

sam: proposed mitigations: 1) introduce a comm_pool (persistent slab) per node with a configurable watermark and borrow/release API so NCCL ephemeral allocations reuse one area. 2) allocator coop: let comm_pool register with main arena so small staging can come from same slab. 3) kv cache view-on-top-of-shard: switch from copy to virtual view where possible.

leo: i prototyped comm_pool yesterday — simple API:
```
struct CommPool { void* base; size_t size; std::atomic<size_t> head; }
void* borrow(size_t bytes) { /* atomic fetch_add + bound check */ }
void release(/* optional */) { /* bump watermark */ }
```
Bench: reusing comm_pool cut NCCL temp allocs by ~60% in my microbench.

alex: nice. what about multi-stream safety? NCCL may overlap kernels and we need per-ring double-buffering. can pool satisfy that without growing too big?

mina: idea: pool provides multiple fixed-size slots = num_rings * pipeline_depth. each borrow returns a slot index. pool size = slot_size * num_slots. that prevents runtime fragmentation and avoids per-request allocation cost.

sam: eviction policy for long-running requests? if a request holds a slot long (large seq), we could block or fall back to allocating ephemeral via cudaMalloc to avoid starving others. need metrics on slot hold times.

alex: on allocator fragmentation: we can tune workspace sizing heuristics. instead of allocating exact needed small chunks, we pad to granularity (e.g., 256KB) and reuse freed ranges. reduces meta-overhead of many tiny allocations.

mina: also saw a pattern where staging buffers created for CPU->GPU async copy were allocated on different streams causing per-stream caches to keep separate buckets. patch to centralize staging allocator per-device reduced duplicate buckets in my run.

leo: KV cache change: we can implement a per-shard pointer table that points into a shared device slab (global kv_base). during shard-build we fill pointers not copy data. writes will do small in-place updates gated by an atomic per-key to keep consistency across TP shards.

sam: caveat: that adds cross-shard synchronization cost on writes (e.g., when extending past seq length). maybe only enable view-on-top for read-only prefix caching and fallback to copy for write-heavy flows.

alex: good pragmatic approach. can we quantify expected memory savings? rough calc: in our test with 2048 batch tokens prefix we saw 3.1GB saved by switching copy->view. with comm_pool + padded workspace ~2.8GB saved. combined ~6GB on 80GB cards which is nontrivial.

mina: action items: 
- leo: open PR for comm_pool prototype (slot-based) + unit tests. label eng-runtime/alloc.
- sam: add allocator padding config and central staging allocator, include perf microbench.
- alex: work with infra to run a node-level soak on 8x config to gather slot hold time histograms (infra-bot to schedule).
- mina: update KV cache behavior doc and add feature flag for view-on-top.

infra-bot: job scheduled: perf-soak/8xA100/comm-pool-hist-1961234620 (ETA ~2h) :robot_face:

leo: filing PR today. will link benchmark in thread when ready.

alex: sweet. if everyone agrees let's aim to land experimental flags behind rollout and watch memory+tail-latency. cc @product maybe for perf-risk note. :+1:

mina: yep. will sync after soak results. thanks! :rocket:
